findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project list, which is randomized per process and can collide
findings.body: The cache key embeds hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python's hash() for ints is deterministic, but the tuple hash is not guaranteed stable across processes and can collide; a collision would return another project set's eligibility for this org. The key also ignores that eligibility depends on the allowlist option, so a stale value can persist for 60s. Use the sorted project ids joined as a string instead.

findings.title: Cached eligibility is returned without re-checking, and cache.get of False is treated as hit
findings.body: The cache stores is_eligible and the cached path returns cached_result and transform check. This is consistent, but the cache is keyed only by org and project ids, not by the dataset/request, and the allowlist is also re-read fresh elsewhere, so the 'fresh' docstring contradicts the caching added in this PR. Behavior differs between cache hit and miss within the 60s window, producing inconsistent results for identical queries.

findings.title: Allowlist membership compares ints against option values that may be strings
findings.body: project_id in allowlist assumes the option stores integer ids. If the option is stored as strings (common for options edited via UI/JSON), no project matches and upsampling silently never applies; if types mismatch in the other direction, the check fails silently. The membership test should normalize types.

findings.title: count() rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count' changes result semantics and may break aliasing
findings.body: The transform replaces count() with an aliased function call regardless of whether the query's orderby, equations, or top-events column references 'count()'. Callers that look up the result by 'count()' key or pass the transformed columns into equations/orderby will break. The alias 'count' also may collide with a user-specified column of the same name.

findings.title: upsampled_count ignores sample_weight existence and returns sum without guaranteeing column
findings.body: The function assumes sample_weight exists for every event in allowlisted projects, but events without the context (for example, older SDKs or events stored before the change) have no sample_weight, so sum() undercounts them to zero or fails the query. The comment asserts a schema guarantee that the code does not enforce. The function also declares required_args=[] and default_result_type 'number' while it is used as an aggregate with the toInt64 wrapper, which truncates fractional sample weights.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility check runs on every _get_event_stats call, including per-bucket sub-queries
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is invoked at the top of _get_event_stats, which is called multiple times per request (split-query flow, transaction queries). Each call does a cache round trip and option lookup, undermining the claimed performance optimization. The comment 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' is misleading since the value is recomputed per call.

findings.title: Top-events path transforms columns but the non-top-events path reuses the same final_columns variable incorrectly
findings.body: final_columns is reassigned inside the RPC branch and the standard branch, but the upsampling transformation is applied to query_columns each time from the original input, so the behavior is correct only because the branches are exclusive. The duplicated transform blocks are fragile; a future edit that applies the transform earlier would double-transform. Hoisting one transformation is safer.

findings.title: Error message text changed for existing clients
findings.body: The response detail for topEvents <= 0 changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is an unrelated behavior change in an upsampling PR that may break clients or tests matching the old string.

findings.title: Docstrings and comments claim performance and consistency guarantees that are not true
findings.body: Docstrings say the cache is 'safe because eventual consistency is acceptable' and that allowlist reads are 'fresh each time', which contradict each other and the caching added here. invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called, so allowlist changes are not reflected for up to 60 seconds.

findings.title: Factory silently swallows all exceptions when setting sample_rate
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps reads and conversions in bare 'except Exception: pass', hiding malformed test data and making tests pass or fail for the wrong reason. It also sets sample_rate on every stored event in test factories, which changes behavior of all tests that use store_event with error_sampling context.

findings.title: Test setUp overwrites self.user and the authed user, and asserts counts that depend on upsampling not yet verified
findings.body: setUp calls login_as(self.user) then reassigns self.user to a new user, so the logged-in user differs from self.user used in the event tags. The count assertions expect 10 for upsampled buckets (1 event at 0.1 rate) but nothing in the store path shows sample_weight is written, so these expectations are unverified and likely fail or pass for the wrong reason.

findings.title: Transaction test asserts count of 1 for the transaction bucket without verifying the transaction was indexed
findings.body: The transaction event is stored with a fixed trace id and no wait_for_event_count, so the snuba query can race and the assertions on data[0] and data[1] are flaky. The test also does not check the transaction path actually bypassed upsampling.

findings.title: Stray 'sentry-repo' submodule file and 'Test 3' PR description
findings.body: The PR adds a submodule pointer file 'sentry-repo' pointing at the base commit, and the description is 'Test 3'. These are unrelated artifacts that should not be merged into the repository.
